subject: Reserved capacity tenor - request for a GPU-cost cushion clause
messages:
From: Alicia Brooks <alicia.brooks@brightlane.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightlane.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity tenor - cushion request given GPU cost volatility

Karthik — thanks for walking us through the Dedicated offering this week. The execs at Brightlane asked us to confirm one thing before we move to commercial: given current GPU market swings, would Redwood consider a short-term "cushion" or price-reset clause tied to a published GPU index for the first 12 months of the reserved commitment?

Specifically, they want: a) a floor on per-token pricing if GPU market spot goes up more than 18% vs baseline; or b) a one-time rebate if GPU index drops by >20% and Brightlane commits to a 24-month term. They are open to either approach but want to understand whether Redwood can accommodate risk-sharing without requiring a full exec waiver.

We have the RFP and initial SOW attached. Can you share what flexibility you have on conditional discounts, the approval path, and what triggers would be operationally feasible?

Thanks — Alicia
Alicia Brooks
Head of Cloud Procurement, Brightlane Health
A: +1 415 555 0123

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Brooks <alicia.brooks@brightlane.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity tenor - cushion request given GPU cost volatility

Alicia — thanks for the clear ask and the docs (received). Quick summary from our side and next steps:

1) Short answer: we can structure a conditional pricing mechanism, but the specifics change whether it is a rebate (post-facto) or a binding floor/ceiling during the contract.

2) Operational constraints: our reserved pricing is tied to committed SKU mix and capacity pool. Any indexation clause that references a third-party GPU index will require Finance sign-off and Legal to define measurement windows and auditability (we need a deterministic index and a monthly feed). For an automatic rebate on a >20% drop, we would require the customer to commit to the 24-month tenor and agree to a reconciliation cadence (quarterly).

3) Approval path: for movements >10% effective price delta we need approval from Growth-Finance + Head of Revenue; >18% requires CRO+Finance exec review. Marcus, can you run a quick sensitivity using the attached commit-pricing-model.csv and show P&L impact for the two options Alicia proposed? Neha / Legal — please flag any standard prohibitions on index referencing (we've had some limits around using raw spot as an index).

Operationally, we also have a standard fallback: ability to route overflow traffic to a lower-cost model variant (quantized) with customer opt-in for quality impact. If Brightlane wants a hard floor tied to our cost, that becomes a bespoke arrangement.

I'll schedule a 30-min sync next week to go through numbers. Attaching a draft SOW to iterate on triggers.

Cheers,
Karthik
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Brooks <alicia.brooks@brightlane.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 09:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity tenor - cushion request given GPU cost volatility

Karthik / team — ran a sensitivity on the attached commit-pricing-model.csv. High level findings:

- Baseline: Brightlane committed spend = $1.2M/year based on current SKU mix (A100-equivalent).
- Scenario A (floor if GPU index increases >18%): Redwood's incremental risk is potential margin compression of ~6-9% over year 1 depending on utilization variance. That would typically justify a mid-single-digit price uplift (3-5%) on the committed rate to compensate for tail risk.
- Scenario B (rebate if GPU index drops >20% and 24mo term): this lowers Brightlane's effective price but transfers upside risk back to Redwood; the expected rebate accrual is modest (<2% expected value) but creates balance-sheet timing considerations (we'd need to accrue reserves quarterly).

Recommendation: 1) Offer a hybrid: a capped floor-trigger where we apply a 3% premium to the committed rate and cap rebate exposure at 2% annually if index falls below threshold. 2) Define the index as the 'OpenCompute GPU Spot Index' (monthly average) and set a 30-day smoothing window to avoid transient spikes. 3) Add a maximum annual reconciliation cap and require Brightlane to accept the lower-quality fall-back routing for overflow in extreme upsides.

I'll prepare a short memo with P&L delta and approval ask for Finance. If this sounds acceptable, we can present the hybrid as the commercial starting point.

—Marcus
Director, Finance (Revenue Ops) | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Brooks <alicia.brooks@brightlane.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Bcc:
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity tenor - cushion request given GPU cost volatility

Alicia — appreciate the patience while we modeled this. We can propose the hybrid Marcus outlined: 3% premium on committed rates (applies only to year 1 base committed units) plus a rebate cap of 2% annually if the agreed index falls >20% below baseline. Index definition will be the OpenCompute GPU Spot Index (monthly avg) with a 30-day smoothing window.

Next steps I propose:
- Laura / Legal to add the clause language to the draft SOW (attached) with the exact trigger language and reconciliation cadence.
- Finance (Marcus) to prepare an approval memo for Growth-Finance and CRO that outlines the worst-case margin impact and accounting treatment.
- Joint call with Brightlane (30 min) Tues 09/22 to walk the hybrid and accept the SOW wording.

Alicia — can you confirm availability on 09/22 10:00-10:30 PT? Also confirm whether Brightlane prefers a rebate payment (backdated credit) or a future invoice credit. That will change accounting treatment.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this with a path that protects both sides.

Best,
Karthik
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
